messages:
ashley: Heads up — canary p99 jumped ~2.5x in eu-west a10+l4 pool after we started rollout of v2.3.1 canary (canary/2026-03-17). H100 clusters look fine. Pausing rollout for now.

infra-bot: Deploy canary/2026-03-17 to eu-west-a10-l4 paused by ashley at 2026-03-17T14:08:41Z :pause_button:

jia: On it. grabbing flame/profiler traces and netstats. which trace id?

ashley: trace id 8f3a2b4c; logs: https://console.internal/trace/8f3a2b4c (curl works: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.internal/api/trace/8f3a2b4c`)

omar: quick scan: PR #5127 touched kernel selector + batching heuristics; commit 7c9b2d4 changed batch delay when kv_cache miss > 20%. that lands right before the canary. probable suspect.

mike: I reproduced locally on an A10-like perf rig. microbench shows higher avg batch delay and more kernel fallback. profiler snippet:
```
kv_cache.miss_rate=0.28
avg_batch_delay_ms: baseline=4.2 -> canary=16.8
kernel_path: optimized_attention_v2 -> fallback_attention_generic
cpu_time/op +48%
```

jia: netstats from the canary machines show NIC tx queue length spikes and small tx drops (~0.3%) around the latency bursts. logs: `net_dev.tx_dropped=0.003` and `tcp_retransmits` ticked up. fits a model where slower per-request kernels cause queueing on A10 NICs.

ashley: interesting — H100 path avoids the fallback (more on-chip memory, different kernel selection), which explains why H100 wasn't impacted. good signal.

omar: plan: 1) pin kernel-selector to previous version for canary to confirm 2) open rollback PR for selector change 3) run synthetic canary load with perf-ci. I opened PR #5134 to pin. Use this flag to force-old-selector: `--kernel-selector=legacy-2026-02`

perf-ci: Synthetic canary run (baseline v2.3.0 vs v2.3.1 canary) replicated p99 ~1.7x increase on a10-l4 mix under target traffic. Trace ids: 8f3a2b4c (canary) / 8f3a0c11 (baseline).

mike: if pin fixes it we revert 7c9b2d4 and rework batching heuristic. Suggest adding a regression test that simulates high kv cache miss ratio + mixed-hardware profile.

ashley: I'll request immediate rollback of the selector change and schedule a 30-min watch after rollback. creating rollback request now. assigning @sre-oncall to monitor p50/p99, NIC drops, and tcp retransmits.

sre-oncall: On it — I'll watch the dashboards and set alerts for p99 > 1.2x baseline and tx_dropped > 0.1%. will report if anything spikes after rollback.

ashley: thanks. if rollback confirms, we'll hold rollout until a fix + additional perf CI is green.

(threads: next steps -> revert PR 5140 if rollback successful; follow-up: add regression harness and tighten kernel selector canary gating)
